summary: The agent implemented the new module and passed all baseline tests, but 20 of 361 new tests failed. Most failures come from sorting legitimate multi-valued DICOM attributes, with one separate dimension-index renumbering defect.

details.reasoning: The implementation is substantial and legitimate, but sort_frames compares raw pydicom MultiValue objects with '<'. ImagePositionPatient is a valid multi-valued key, and this causes 19 sorting-related tests to raise MultiFrameError instead of sorting. The implementation also returns early from dimension normalization when DimensionIndexSequence is absent, leaving DimensionIndexValues at their original values in the documented partial-frame-content case.
details.secondary_factors: The agent changed only src/pydicom/__init__.py and src/pydicom/multiframe.py; no test manipulation or stubbing was detected. Full-suite validation was also interrupted by an unrelated TLS certificate-path problem.

quick_failure_summary: New tests fail because sorting cannot order MultiValue attributes and one derivation skips required dimension-index renumbering.

justification.issue_description: sort_frames does not support the multi-valued DICOM attributes it is required to order, and dimension normalization skips renumbering when no dimension description sequence is present.
justification.evidence: The prompt requires sort_frames to put frames in ascending order of key values and accepts any attribute name or tag. The failing key is ImagePositionPatient, whose pydicom value is MultiValue. The agent trace explicitly tested that MultiValue '<' raises TypeError, while src/pydicom/multiframe.py:367 still executes 'a < b'. The prompt also explicitly requires remaining dimension values to be renumbered; the implementation returns at line 425 when DimensionIndexSequence is absent, producing [6] instead of [1].
justification.verdict_reasoning: This is an agent-side missed requirement, not an undocumented verifier convention. Multi-valued DICOM attributes are a foreseeable class of attribute values for a generic attribute-key API, and the agent verified the exact comparison failure during its own run. The dimension behavior is also stated directly in the task. The dominant defect is the sorting implementation, so FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT is more appropriate than a test-mismatch or environment verdict.

problem_assessment.notes: The task is dense but specifies the required ordering, validation, derivation, provenance, and dimension rules. The new tests are deterministic and exercise a challenging but solvable feature; vector-valued DICOM attributes and partial dimension metadata are reasonably foreseeable.

evidence: JUnit reports baseline 2632 tests passed with 0 failures and new tests 341 passed with 20 failures; the new failures reach src/pydicom/multiframe.py rather than failing during collection or bootstrap.

The test log reports the agent’s full-suite validation stopped after 682 passes at test_fetch_data_files because certifi pointed to the invalid CA bundle path /usr/local/lib/python3.12/site-packages/certifi/cacert.pem.

The trajectory shows the agent spent a full 97.52-second suite run waiting on that unrelated failure, then performed focused checks; this reduced full-suite validation coverage but did not explain the deterministic new-test failures.
The agent trajectory’s MultiValue probe observed TypeError for '<' between MultiValue instances, directly confirming the main implementation defect.
environment_assessment.finding: The environment has a broken TLS CA-bundle path that interrupts full-suite validation, but the feature verifier itself runs correctly and exposes independent implementation failures.
